definition: To describe, outline, or mark out the specific boundaries or steps of a biological pathway with precision.
etymology: From Latin delineatus, past participle of delineare ('to sketch out, trace').
manuscriptExample: High-resolution cryo-EM allowed us to delineate the atomic contact residues between the spike protein and receptor.
conferenceExample: Reviewer 3 recommended rewriting Section 2.4 to better delineate inclusion criteria for patient cohorts.

definition: A division or contrast between two states represented as being opposed or distinct.
etymology: From Ancient Greek διχοτομία (dichotomía, 'a cutting in two').
manuscriptExample: Our findings reconcile the longstanding dichotomy between genetic predisposition and environmental drivers.
conferenceExample: In the rebuttal, we clarified that M1/M2 macrophage states present a continuous spectrum rather than a rigid dichotomy.
